THE_BLOCKER.providerError: tools.0.custom: For 'array' type, property 'maxItems' is not supported
THE_BLOCKER.rootCause: §196's vNext schema emits `maxItems: 0` on unresolvedFactDeclarations.items.properties.governedEvidenceSourceIds whenever no governed evidence was supplied, so that a model with no governed records has no legal way to name one. Anthropic's strict tool-schema mode rejects `maxItems` on an array and refuses the whole request.
THE_BLOCKER.whyNotCaughtEarlier: `stripAnthropicUnsupportedKeywords` (§108) removes `minLength` and `minItems` only. Its own comment records that no `maxItems` existed in the schema at the time it was written. §196 introduced the first one and nothing connected the new keyword to the adapter. §196's suite passed 91/91 because it tested the schema as a DOCUMENT; the strip only matters for the schema as a REQUEST.
THE_BLOCKER.diagnosisMethod: all twelve request bodies rebuilt offline and their schema keywords compared against v15's, which has executed hosted many times. Exactly one keyword is introduced by vNext — `maxItems` — occurring once per row. Stripping it removes exactly one keyword kind and touches no property, type, enum, required list or description. ZERO further provider calls were made to establish this.

WHAT_THIS_FALSIFIES.section196_caseK3: K3 asserted 'with no governed evidence supplied, the wire schema forbids naming one at all' and summarised the design as 'transport refuses it, and the boundary refuses it again'. On the actual hosted transport the FIRST HALF DOES NOT HOLD: the transport does not refuse the id, it refuses the entire request.
WHAT_THIS_FALSIFIES.whatStillHolds: The BOUNDARY half is untouched. §196 cases K1 and K2 refuse an unsupplied governed sourceId at the projection, deterministically. The safety property survives; the claimed SECOND LAYER does not.
WHAT_THIS_FALSIFIES.honestRestatement: the two-layer claim was correct about the schema as a document and wrong about the schema as a request. A structural guarantee that cannot be transmitted to the provider is not a structural guarantee on the hosted path.
WHAT_THIS_FALSIFIES.section196RemainsOtherwiseIntact: the other 90 of §196's 91 cases are unaffected: they concern the projection, identity, provenance, multi-gap isolation, the citation reuse rule and the reconstruction invariants, none of which this defect touches.

CANDIDATE_CORRECTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.change: extend the §108 Anthropic compatibility strip to remove `maxItems`, as it already removes `minLength` and `minItems`
CANDIDATE_CORRECTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.effect: the request becomes transportable; `governedEvidenceSourceIds` becomes an unbounded string array, so a model COULD emit an id and the projection would refuse it as GOVERNED_SOURCE_ID_NOT_IN_SUPPLIED_SET
CANDIDATE_CORRECTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.keeps: the boundary-level guarantee, which is where this product's protection has always actually lived
CANDIDATE_CORRECTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.size: smallest change; squarely the §108 precedent applied to a third keyword
CANDIDATE_CORRECTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.requires: a fresh successor preregistration — every per-row wireSchemaSha256 moves

CANDIDATE_CORRECTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.change: omit `governedEvidenceSourceIds` entirely when the supplied set is empty, rather than bounding it at zero
CANDIDATE_CORRECTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.effect: no `maxItems` is ever emitted, and a model given no governed evidence has NO FIELD AT ALL to put an id in
CANDIDATE_CORRECTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.keeps: a guarantee STRONGER than maxItems:0, and one the transport accepts
CANDIDATE_CORRECTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.size: a vNext PROTOCOL REVISION, not a transport workaround; makes the declaration item shape vary by request, which the schema already does for enums
CANDIDATE_CORRECTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.requires: a vNext protocol revision plus a fresh successor preregistration

CANDIDATE_CORRECTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.change: always supply the row's real governed sourceIds
CANDIDATE_CORRECTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.effect: rows with governed evidence get an enum; rows with none still need A or B

myReading: B is the better architecture and A is the smaller change. The choice turns on whether the transport-level guarantee is worth a protocol revision. §197 DOES NOT MAKE THAT CHOICE.

SECOND_FINDING_PRE_SPEND.consequence: the binding cannot be legitimately populated at the first pass today
SECOND_FINDING_PRE_SPEND.howSection197HandledIt: the governed-evidence families were scoped to the VERIFIER stage, where buildVerifierV3UserPrompt renders {sourceId, text} verbatim with citations intact — which is where §195 found the collision and where v3.3 actually lives. That scoping is sound and needs no change.
SECOND_FINDING_PRE_SPEND.whatRemainsOpen: a future protocol revision that closes the first-pass binding must decide whether to expose sourceIds to the first pass without exposing citations. §197 does not decide it.
